newsitem.title: UK: HSBC leads sector up as Hong Kong rallies.
newsitem.headline: HSBC leads sector up as Hong Kong rallies.

text.p: Shares in HSBC Holdings Plc and Standard Chartered Plc led an already buoyant UK banking sector higher on Tuesday, after Hong Kong's Hang Seng share index scaled new peaks overnight, dealers said.
Shares in HSBC surged 41p, or more than two percent, to 2041-1/2p at 0810 GMT, just 1/2p off the record high set initially.
Both stocks have large exposure to Hong Kong, where the benchmark Hang Seng rose 116.30 points to 15,487.24.
Shares in National Westminster Bank, however, sank 9-1/2p to 849 after Dresdner Kleinwort Benson told its clients to switch out of NatWest shares and into Barclays Plc, dealers said.
The analyst at the brokerage couldn't immediately be reached to comment.
Shares in Barclays climbed 14-1/2p to 1248-1/2, while shares in Lloyds TSB Group rose 11-1/2p to 686-1/2.
The rally in the bank sector, said one dealer, reflected a lack of fresh ideas among investors.
"With only a few exceptions, people feel confident in the same sectors that have been outperforming the market for months now," said one dealer.

"We've been led by the pharmaceuticals and financial sectors and until we see some improvement in manufacturing and engineering, people are going to stick with the visible earners. I don't think it's anymore sophisticated than that," he added.
Others also pointed to ongoing speculation of consolidation within the industry. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
